intro: In Spanish every thing has its gender: some words take el, others take la. Today you learn how to tell.
b1.titulo: The article goes with the noun
b1.texto:
In Spanish every noun is either masculine or feminine, and the article goes with it:

- **el** libro, **un** libro (masculine)
- **la** mesa, **una** mesa (feminine)
- **los** libros, **las** mesas (plural)

Usually words ending in **-o** are masculine and words ending in **-a** are feminine. But not always:

- **el mapa**, **el problema** (they end in -a and are masculine)
- **la mano** (it ends in -o and is feminine)

Also, feminine nouns that begin with a stressed **a** take **el**: **el agua**. But they are still feminine: **las aguas**.
b4.titulo: El agua, la mano and el mapa
b4.texto:
Some words trick you. Look at these three cases:

- **el agua**: it is feminine, but it begins with a stressed «a» and that is why it takes **el**. In the plural it goes back to normal: **las aguas**.
- **la mano**: it ends in -o, but it is feminine.
- **el mapa** and **el problema**: they end in -a, but they are masculine.

The ending helps, but the article has the last word.
b6.pregunta: How do you say «the books» in Spanish?
b6.o0.refuerzo: Correct: libro is masculine and the plural is los libros.
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Las» is feminine, and libro is masculine.
b6.o2.refuerzo: The noun goes in the plural too: libros.
b7.o0.refuerzo: «Mapa» is masculine, even though it ends in -a.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «La» is feminine, and mapa is not.
b9.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «The problem is big».
p.el libro.consejo: It ends in -o: it is masculine.
p.la mesa.consejo: It ends in -a: it is feminine.
p.el mapa.consejo: Careful! It ends in -a but it is masculine: «el mapa».
p.la mano.consejo: Careful! It ends in -o but it is feminine: «la mano».
p.el agua.consejo: It is feminine, but it begins with a stressed a and takes «el». In the plural: «las aguas».
p.el problema.consejo: It ends in -a but it is masculine, like many Greek words.
p.grande.consejo: It does not change with gender: «un libro grande», «una mesa grande».
p.pequeña.consejo: Feminine form. With a feminine noun: «la mesa pequeña».
p.pequeño.consejo: Masculine form. With a masculine noun: «el libro pequeño».
p.el libro de Ana.consejo: «De» is used to say who something belongs to.
b5.f0.texto: The teacher leaves a big map and an old book on the table.
b5.f1.texto: Ana says that the map is small, and everyone laughs because it takes up half the table.
b5.f2.texto: Lucía points at it with her hand and explains that in Spain you say «el mapa», even though it ends in a.
b5.f5.texto: At the end of the class the book goes back to its shelf and the map stays rolled up in a corner.
b5.f6.texto: On the table there is only a glass of cold water.
b5.f7.texto: Ana looks at it and thinks that el agua is a bit tricky too: it takes el and it is feminine.
b5.f8.texto: But that will be for another day.
